Plot a rarefaction of a statistic

Source: R/sampling.R
plot.trait_rarefaction.Rd

Draws the mean of each statistic from trait_rarefaction() against sampling effort, with the interval over subsamples as a band, one panel per statistic. Dashed vertical lines mark reference levels of effort: for a rarefaction over cover, by default the published rule of measuring at least the species that make up 80% of the vegetation (Pakeman & Quested 2007). No such rule is drawn by default for the number of individuals per population; give it in reference when the field or study has one.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'trait_rarefaction'
plot(
  x,
  reference = NULL,
  colours = "#0072B2",
  alpha = 0.25,
  scales = "free_y",
  ...,
  colour = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Result of trait_rarefaction().

reference

Levels of effort marked by dashed lines; named values are written next to the lines. NULL (the default) marks the 80% rule for cover and nothing for n; FALSE draws no line.

colours

Colour of the line and band; the default is the blue of the Okabe-Ito palette.

alpha

Transparency of the band.

scales

Passed to ggplot2::facet_wrap().

...

Not used.

colour

Deprecated; use colours, as in the other plots.

Value

A ggplot object.

References

Pakeman, R. J., & Quested, H. M. (2007). Sampling plant functional traits: what proportion of the species need to be measured? Applied Vegetation Science, 10, 91–96. doi:10.1111/j.1654-109x.2007.tb00507.x

See also

trait_rarefaction().

Examples

set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(paste0("s", 1:5), each = 40),
                  species = sample(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), 200, TRUE, prob = c(5, 3, 1, 1)))
ind$trait <- c(a = 10, b = 12, c = 15, d = 18)[ind$species] + rnorm(200)
plot(trait_rarefaction(ind, n = 2:10, reps = 10))

plot(trait_rarefaction(ind, cover = seq(0.3, 1, by = 0.1)))

# a rule of the study, for the number of individuals
plot(trait_rarefaction(ind, n = 2:10, reps = 10), reference = c("protocol" = 5))
